subsystems.name: Reactor core
subsystems.role: contains the fission fuel, sustains the chain reaction, and transfers heat to hydrogen propellant flowing through channels.
parts: fuel elements (uranium carbide or nitride in a refractory matrix)

subsystems.name: Propellant feed system
subsystems.role: stores and pumps liquid hydrogen into the reactor at high pressure.

subsystems.name: Nozzle and thrust structure
subsystems.role: expands the hot hydrogen gas to produce thrust and transmits thrust to the vehicle.

subsystems.name: Radiation shielding
subsystems.role: protects crew and sensitive components from reactor neutrons and gamma rays.
parts: shadow shield (e.g. lithium hydride or tungsten)

subsystems.name: Control and instrumentation
subsystems.role: monitors and controls reactor power and propellant flow.

buildSteps.title: Design the reactor core
buildSteps.detail: Use neutronics and thermal-hydraulic models to size fuel elements, moderator and control drums for the required power and thrust.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate fuel elements
buildSteps.detail: Form uranium carbide or nitride kernels, coat them to resist hydrogen corrosion, and assemble them into hexagonal or cylindrical elements with coolant channels.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the core
buildSteps.detail: Stack fuel elements with moderator and install control drums inside a pressure vessel.

buildSteps.title: Build the propellant system
buildSteps.detail: Install turbopumps, valves and cryogenic plumbing to feed liquid hydrogen at high pressure.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the nozzle
buildSteps.detail: Attach a regeneratively cooled nozzle that uses some hydrogen to cool the throat before the gas enters the core.

buildSteps.title: Add shielding and controls
buildSteps.detail: Place a shadow shield between the reactor and the crew compartment, and wire neutron detectors and control systems.

buildSteps.title: Ground test
buildSteps.detail: Fire the engine on a test stand with hydrogen exhaust, measuring thrust and specific impulse, as was done in the NERVA program.

buildSteps.title: Flight qualification
buildSteps.detail: After ground tests, integrate the engine with a stage and perform uncrewed flight tests in space.

prerequisites.why: fuel must survive hydrogen at thousands of kelvin without corroding or cracking; NERVA tested some designs but none have flown.
existing rocket turbopumps handle liquid hydrogen, but must be adapted for nuclear heating and long-duration storage.
shielding must protect crew without adding excessive mass; designs exist but are not flight-proven for nuclear thermal propulsion.

prerequisites.tech: Space nuclear reactor control and safety
prerequisites.why: reactor control systems exist for power reactors and submarines, but space qualification and launch safety are still being developed.
liquid hydrogen boils off over time; long-duration storage and transfer are needed for Mars missions.

pathway.milestone: Ground prototype tests of fuel elements and reactor cores
pathway.unlocks: data on materials performance and reactor dynamics.

pathway.milestone: Full-power ground test of a flight-like engine
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the engine can operate at required thrust and specific impulse.
proof of restart, throttling and thermal management in vacuum.

pathway.milestone: Crewed Mars transit using nuclear thermal propulsion
pathway.unlocks: faster transits and lower radiation exposure for crews.
